curated.instructions: omr/instructions/8261-1-1.pdf (one book; no page of functions)

functions.does: The 12 tooth gear on the roof steers the front wheels: it turns a vertical shaft down through the cab, whose 12 tooth bevel gear at the foot turns the 20 tooth gear on a shaft running forward under the truck; a knob gear at that shaft's front end turns the knob gear on the front axle's steering post, swinging its steering arm, which pushes the tie rod that turns both front wheels.
functions.source: book: steps 17-18 (vertical shaft, knob gears), 20 (front axle), 21 (20 tooth gear) and 36 (roof); inferred: the book draws no arrow, the drive is worked out from the gears

functions.does: The rear wheels ride on a trailing arm: two bent beams pivot on a 7-long axle under the middle of the truck and carry the rear wheels' stub axles at the back, so the rear wheels rise and fall together, the shock absorber squeezing.
functions.source: inferred: from the model file (the rear axle's sub-assembly hangs on bent beams pivoting on a 7-long axle, with a shock absorber behind); the book draws no arrow, and the step that fits the shock absorber isn't identified
functions.note: how far the arm can swing is set by the shock absorber's travel; its two ends swing a little on their pins as the arm moves. lifted: the text has the wheel or arm moved ("so the rear wheels rise and fall together"), so it is worked with the model held in the hand, the frame still and no tyre on the ground, its own shock absorber giving through its travel; p55 moves: the pivot axle goes through the axle holes at the ends of both bent beams, so it turns with the arm (booklet step 13, page 9) (Erik signed it, "Sign suspension lists", 2026-11-15)

functions.does: The shock absorber's spring pushes the rear wheels back down.
functions.skip: a spring only matters under gravity or force

functions.does: The four wheels roll freely; there's no drive.

questions.question: Is the front axle pendular?
questions.answer: No. Function 2 dropped (Erik signed it, "Drop 8261 function 2", 2026-11-15): "The front axle swings side to side about the steering shaft it hangs from, so the front wheels can follow rough ground; the steering still works as it swings." Booklet steps 20 and 21 (https://www.lego.com/cdn/product-assets/product.bi.core.pdf/4548627.pdf#page=14 to #page=16) hold the front axle fast in the chassis on two pins and the steering axle; it steers at its hubs and doesn't swing. The model's front axle differs from the booklet: a 180 degree connector p85 32034 with two 43093 (p84, p86) on top and no pins up from the top beam, and the 33299 on a 4L axle, not the 6L steering axle; that difference may become an erratum. The functions after it moved up one number.

hold.reason: The booklet shows the roof shaft steering to full lock (https://www.lego.com/cdn/product-assets/product.bi.core.pdf/4548627.pdf#page=32), but in the viewer p131 stops at 0.105 rad each way, at a part against itself (193/193 and 191/191); the check turns 1.47 rad. Viewer sweep on today's code, decision 298.
